parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs a national universal-exposure document/entry regime with a hostile division layer. National rules bar marker self-selection, halted X markers, and instruct officers to refuse cases where records cast 'reasonable doubt' on sex, with lifetime fraud ineligibility considered; trans travellers report blocked passports and stranding, and eight-plus governments issued advisories. Litigation is unresolved and the Supreme Court let the regime take effect, so no working remedy is documented. Custody is documented as harsh (conversion-therapy policy, immigration abuse, birth-sex placement). The division adds care bans for minors and all Medicaid patients, a custody care funding bar, sports and surgical document rules, and no gender-identity nondiscrimination law — offset by a gender-identity hate-crime statute, functioning courts, sanctuary cities, and no documented identity-based violence.

entry_documents.exposure: National order ended marker self-selection and X markers; cable instructs refusal where records cast reasonable doubt on sex and allows fraud/lifetime-ineligibility review; travellers report passports blocked and stranded abroad. Division requires surgery or court order for birth-certificate change and reverted licence-marker policy to surgery documentation.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports valid until expiry; fraud finding is never automatic with limited waiver; suit pending in national courts; legal-aid FAQ exists.
entry_documents.interaction: Division document rigidity feeds national screening doubt: a visitor's home passport mismatch meets an officer instructed to refuse, with no division remedy reaching the border.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections bureau adopted conversion-therapy-style policy (hair cutting, hormone removal) from 2026; immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse of trans men; prisoner census withheld since 2025. Division HB 2009 (2 July 2026) bars transition-care funding in its prisons with no taper.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Hate-crime statute covers gender identity; courts have enjoined several national orders; some comparable custody-care bans blocked nationally.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: An outed visitor stopped for document or facility issues enters a custody system where placement and care follow birth sex at both levels.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Facility bans cover all government buildings in 10 units, schools-plus in 9 more, schools-only in 3; 4 units criminalise use under circumstances; 6 extend to some private settings. One documented arrest (19 March 2025) with 24 hours in a men's ward. Whether the division has a ban is not stated.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Trespass statute requires willful entry plus refusal to leave, not automatic arrest; 29 units plus capital district have no mapped ban.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: A visitor using a restroom in a capitol, museum or school building risks trespass exposure magnified by federal birth-sex framing; state remedies do not reach federal buildings.

care_services.exposure: Division SAFE Act bars under-18 transition care, bars Medicaid payment at any age, exposes providers to licence loss and 15-year suits, upheld unanimously January 2026, with a 2026 ballot push to make permanent; a tipline invites reports of 'gender transition interventions.'
care_services.protection: Emergency and non-transition care not documented as denied; two sanctuary cities declared; prior adult-care restrictive order was blocked and withdrawn.
care_services.interaction: A trans minor travelling with a guardian in the division can obtain no transition care from any provider, and care-seeking risks provider reporting under the tipline climate.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy (May 2026) prioritises neutralising groups 'radically pro-transgender'; justice department rhetoric labels care 'mutilation' and directs investigation of 'gender ideology'; reward guidance references the phrase contextually; 66% of residents back birth-sex document laws (2025 poll).
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Reward criteria never list the phrase; same document says counterterrorism powers will not target mere disagreement; DOJ orders blocked or withdrawn in litigation.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing raises both outing probability and severity at every state-federal encounter, while partial judicial pushback limits but does not reverse it.

minors_guardians.exposure: Division bans all transition surgery and starting hormones for under-18s with provider liability; national orders direct criminal investigation of schools facilitating social transition and describe youth care as 'mutilation'; sports barred by sex at all school levels through college.
minors_guardians.protection: Those already in treatment may continue; national prosecution order is contested and several orders enjoined; no documented prosecution of a travelling family.
minors_guardians.interaction: A visiting parent with a trans minor loses access to continuation or new care in the division and faces a hostile official climate if the minor is outed at school-adjacent settings.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No dated trans-specific violence incident with outcome in the division is documented; 23 units cover gender identity in bias-crime statutes and 37 lacked such statutes as of 2019; national bias statistics track orientation rather than gender identity.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Both division hate-crime statutes explicitly cover gender identity; no sodomy law; no documented pattern of violence; travel guidance advises checking recent reports.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Adequate criminal-recourse machinery exists for assault, but weak everyday anti-discrimination coverage leaves service refusal and harassment largely unremedied.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport, executive-order and health-rule challenges all unresolved; division document-reversion unlitigated and attributed to an 'unspecified incident'; sunset and ballot-initiative outcomes unknown; division has no gender-identity nondiscrimination law.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Functioning courts: division supreme court and national Supreme Court act; national hate-crime statute, 2020 employment ruling and 2022 marriage statute in force; legal-aid FAQ and equality maps operate.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Which measures are operative at travel time is genuinely open, so exposure fluctuates; courts have delivered real relief on some measures while letting the core document regime stand.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra bars entry to transgender visitors judged noncompliant with no effective remedy — exclusion and humiliation without custody. This dossier's cable-driven refusal on 'reasonable doubt' about sex plus lifetime fraud exposure is comparably exclusionary and similarly lacks a working remedy, but is conditional on a documented discrepancy rather than a register targeting all visibly trans visitors, and functioning courts plus pending litigation soften it. Marginally above 0.35-A.

Vesskar features routine checkpoint exposure, a public-order statute reaching deceptive presentation, lengthy detentions, scarce legal aid and inconsistent enforcement. Here the exposure is at least as universal (documents that cannot be made to match, entry-refusal instruction), plus documented custody abuse — but identity itself is not criminalised, a hate-crime statute covers gender identity, and courts have blocked several measures. Similar level, somewhat higher recourse, somewhat harsher custody.

Kestrel Isles shows secondary screening, discretionary refusal, humiliating delays and slow, rarely revised remedies — administrative only. This dossier's regime matches that friction but exceeds it: an explicit instruction to refuse on sex doubt, lifetime-ineligibility consideration, stranding reports, multiple foreign travel advisories, and documented birth-sex custody with care denial. Worse than 0.55-B, justifying a materially lower score.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller faces one system, not two. A national document and entry regime that cannot be satisfied by a mismatched passport (post-2025 orders, Supreme Court clearance, refusal cable, fraud exposure) is a universal exposure with no documented working remedy; it converts any outing into possible denial of entry, stranding or a lifetime bar. On top, the division layers resident-facing care bans, surgical document rules, a custody care funding bar and no gender-identity nondiscrimination law, and it sits inside a country where facility bans reach government buildings and can be criminal trespass. Mitigation is real but partial: functioning courts, a gender-identity hate-crime statute, sanctuary cities, marriage and employment protections, and no documented identity-based killing. Net: routine friction with credible detention-level harm if outed into custody or a facility dispute — Elevated Risk, near the top of it.
